pack_metadata.title: Urgent cyber-financial-fraud containment and recovery journey
pack_metadata.user_outcome: Contain further loss, create usable bank and police records, pursue the correct transaction-specific dispute path, and reach either evidenced restoration/reversal or documented closure without overstating liability or recovery.
pack_metadata.central_scope: India-wide Central Government, RBI, NPCI and DoT channels, plus necessary regulated actors and explicit State/UT police dependencies.
explicit_exclusions: No guarantee of fund hold, freeze, reversal, zero liability, FIR, arrest, charge-sheet, restoration or recovery.
No state-specific FIR, cyber-police-station, court-release or lien-removal procedure is generalized nationally.
No universal card-network chargeback code or deadline is asserted without the actual issuer and card-network rules.
No enterprise CERT-In reporting workflow, securities-market fraud route, crypto-asset tracing, civil suit, consumer commission case or private insurance claim is fully mapped.
No advice to share OTP, PIN, password, CVV, full card number or other credential secret with any caller, portal or intermediary.

qualifying_questions.question: Is money still moving, is the fraudster still connected, or is there an immediate threat to personal safety?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Ongoing loss requires containment and 1930/bank reporting before slower complaint work; a safety emergency requires 112/local police.
options: Money or access may still be at risk
Fraud has stopped but is recent
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not wait for perfect evidence or classification before cf.t02 and cf.t03. If there is a safety emergency, use 112/local police in parallel.

qualifying_questions.question: For each disputed transaction, what are the exact date/time, amount, reference number and current status?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: NCRP, the bank/issuer, NPCI and RBI CMS need transaction identifiers, and failed-transaction timelines depend on the exact fact pattern.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Unknown fields do not block urgent reporting, but each missing identifier becomes an Action Required item before a transaction-specific claim is treated as complete.

qualifying_questions.question: Did the user personally approve the transaction by entering a UPI PIN, OTP, card authentication or banking password, even because of deception?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: The RBI liability frameworks in this pack govern unauthorised transactions; a victim-authorised scam must not be promised the same result.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Unknown or disputed authorisation blocks any zero-liability conclusion. Immediate containment and reporting continue.

qualifying_questions.question: Which channels and actors are involved?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Bank account, card, UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, ATM, merchant card payment and PPI/wallet routes have different actors and rules.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: The actual bank, issuer, PSP/TPAP, wallet and network must be resolved from the statement/app before channel-specific escalation is presented as complete.

qualifying_questions.question: Was the transaction successful, pending, declined/failed, or is the status inconsistent across the app and bank statement?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: RBI failed-transaction auto-reversal rules do not provide a universal reversal right for a successful fraud transfer.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not apply a T+1 or T+5 failed-transaction timeline until the bank/PSP confirms that the fact pattern matches the RBI definition and row.

qualifying_questions.question: Is the registered phone/SIM lost, stolen, unexpectedly out of service, ported, duplicated, or associated with unknown mobile connections?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: SIM takeover and lost-device cases require the telecom-service-provider and Sanchar Saathi/CEIR branches in addition to financial containment.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: A lost/stolen device enables cf.t14; SIM compromise enables cf.t13. Provider-specific blocking/reissue details remain Action Required until the actual TSP is identified.

qualifying_questions.question: Were credentials shared, a remote-access app installed, email/cloud/social accounts accessed, or the device otherwise compromised?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Further access can continue after the first payment and account recovery is provider-specific.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Potential compromise enables cf.t15; an installed suspicious Android APK materially matching the cited threat enables cf.t21. Do not factory-reset or delete evidence before preserving what police/bank may need unless immediate containment requires isolation.

qualifying_questions.question: In which State/UT was the victim located when the incident occurred, and what is the present contact location?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: NCRP routes complaints to State/UT police and current nodal/grievance contacts are state-specific.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Missing location blocks reliable State/UT routing; do not substitute another state's procedure.

qualifying_questions.question: Has each bank/PSP/card/wallet complaint already been filed, and what are its reference number, filing timestamp, reply and published escalation timeline?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: RBI CMS is not the first complaint forum and its 2026 eligibility clock depends on the regulated-entity complaint and any longer RBI/NPCI/card-network timeline.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: No proof of prior complaint blocks RBI CMS maintainability. A final unsatisfactory reply may enable immediate CMS filing, subject to the 2026 Scheme.

qualifying_questions.question: Has any amount actually been credited back, placed on hold/lien, restored under a police/court process, or only described verbally?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: A hold is not the same as restoration, and a verbal assurance is not completion proof.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Only an account credit plus matching written disposition, or a documented final closure, completes cf.t20.

tasks.title: Immediate: stop further engagement and open a timestamped incident log
tasks.user_goal: Prevent a second payment and preserve an accurate sequence of events while urgent calls begin.
tasks.trigger: Suspected or confirmed cyber-financial fraud, whether payment is ongoing, recent or discovered later.

timelines.label: Start
timelines.value: Immediately on discovery
timelines.applicability: All suspected financial cyber frauds; bank and 1930 reporting should not wait for a polished dossier.

steps: Stop replying to the fraudster and do not send a verification, tax, release or recovery payment.
Record discovery time, transaction time, actors contacted and every reference number in one chronology.
If there is an immediate personal-safety emergency, call 112/local police while another trusted person handles the financial calls.
tasks.tracking: Maintain a contemporaneous incident log; append rather than overwrite prior entries.
tasks.rejection_handling: Not applicable; this is user-controlled containment documentation.
tasks.escalation: Proceed in parallel to cf.t02 and cf.t03; do not wait for cf.t04 or cf.t05.

state_local_dependency.description: 112 and emergency police response are State/UT operated; use only for an actual emergency.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The log proves what the user recorded, not what the bank, fraudster or police did.

tasks.title: Immediate: notify every affected bank, PSP, card issuer or wallet and contain access
tasks.user_goal: Create a timestamped regulated-actor fraud report and block or restrict compromised channels before further debits occur.
tasks.trigger: Any affected account, card, UPI handle, wallet, net-banking/mobile-banking credential or payment instrument.

timelines.label: Unauthorised-transaction notification
timelines.value: At the earliest; 24x7 reporting channels must be available for covered banks/non-bank PPI issuers
timelines.applicability: Covered unauthorised electronic transactions; immediate containment is still prudent for victim-authorised scams.

steps: Use the number in the regulated actor's official app/site, card back or transaction alert; never use a search-ad result or number supplied by the fraudster.

Report the transaction as fraud, state whether the user approved it, and request the actor's available containment action: card block, UPI block, net-banking/mobile-banking disablement, account debit restriction or wallet suspension.
Ask for a complaint/reference number, report timestamp, affected instruments, and written confirmation of what was blocked.
Ask the actor to preserve transaction logs and attempt its available fraud hold/recall/beneficiary-bank coordination without representing that it must succeed.
tasks.tracking: Track each actor separately by complaint number; record promised callback or document deadlines.
tasks.rejection_handling: If the call centre refuses, use the actor's direct online fraud link/app/branch and escalate to its grievance/nodal officer while preserving the refusal details.
tasks.escalation: cf.t18, then cf.t19 when the 2026 RBI CMS eligibility gate is satisfied for a covered regulated entity.

state_local_dependency.description: Regulated-actor containment is separate from police routing.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A complaint or block confirmation does not prove that funds were held or will be reversed.

tasks.title: Immediate: call 1930 for financial cyber fraud
tasks.user_goal: Put the recent transaction into the national CFCFRMS/NCRP response path as quickly as possible.
tasks.trigger: Ongoing or recent cyber-financial fraud; especially when funds may still be traceable in the payment system.

timelines.label: Helpline availability
timelines.applicability: Cyber financial fraud immediate reporting in India.

steps: Call 1930 and identify the incident as financial cyber fraud.
Give the bank/wallet/merchant, transaction reference/UTR if known, date/time, amount, victim mobile and suspect identifiers requested by the operator.
Record the call time, any acknowledgement/login/reference number and the exact instruction for completing the NCRP complaint.
If the call is unanswered, continue cf.t02 and file cf.t06 directly; do not treat an unanswered call as a reason to wait.
tasks.tracking: Use any acknowledgement actually issued in the NCRP journey and incident log; no current nationwide public source verified a universal 1930 caller acknowledgement artifact, helpline-to-portal deadline or caller-facing hold status.
tasks.rejection_handling: If 1930 is unavailable, use https://cybercrime.gov.in and preserve attempted-call evidence.
tasks.escalation: cf.t06, cf.t16 and cf.t17; exact State/UT police action remains local.

state_local_dependency.description: 1930 call centres and subsequent complaint handling involve State/UT police within the national framework.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Calling 1930 does not guarantee a freeze, lien, FIR or recovery.

tasks.title: Immediate: preserve transaction and communication evidence
tasks.user_goal: Keep the material needed by NCRP, the regulated actor and police without exposing credentials.
tasks.trigger: Any suspected cybercrime complaint.
steps: Save bank statements, transaction receipts, alerts, emails, full URLs, chat transcripts, suspect-number screenshots, images and videos before messages/accounts disappear.
Keep original files unchanged where possible and work from copies; note who collected each item and when.
Mask credentials in working summaries, but preserve originals securely for authorised bank/police submission.
Do not send PIN, OTP, password or CVV as evidence.
tasks.tracking: Maintain an evidence index and retain portal-generated hash values for uploaded files where supplied.
tasks.rejection_handling: If an upload is rejected, keep the original, create a compliant copy within the portal's published size/format limits, and record the transformation.
tasks.escalation: Provide evidence only through official bank/portal/police channels; ask the investigating officer before destructive device remediation when forensic value may exist.

state_local_dependency.description: Evidence collection is user-controlled; admissibility and further forensic collection are case-specific.

tasks.fail_closed_note: This task preserves potential evidence; it does not determine authenticity, admissibility or liability.

tasks.title: Gate: classify each transaction without delaying urgent reports
tasks.user_goal: Route each debit to the correct unauthorised, victim-authorised or failed-transaction branch.
tasks.trigger: After urgent containment has begun and transaction evidence is available.
steps: For each debit, record whether the user approved it and how, whether credentials were shared, and whether the actor's systems show success, pending or failure.
Route no-user-approval bank/card debits to cf.t07 and no-user-approval non-bank PPI debits to cf.t08.
Route successful payments approved because of deception to cf.t09 plus the channel task; do not label them zero-liability eligible without the regulated actor's reasoned determination.
Route debited-but-not-completed domestic payment-system events to cf.t10 only when the exact RBI failed-transaction row matches.
tasks.tracking: Maintain a per-transaction classification table and update it when the bank/PSP supplies final status.
tasks.rejection_handling: If facts or actor status conflict, mark the transaction Unknown/Conflict and pursue both the fraud complaint and status enquiry without asserting a liability result.
tasks.escalation: cf.t18 for a written regulated-actor determination; cf.t19 for eligible deficiency-in-service complaints.

state_local_dependency.description: Police may characterize offences, but this gate addresses payment-complaint routing rather than criminal-law classification.

tasks.fail_closed_note: User approval, actor authentication and legal authorisation are not assumed equivalent; disputed classification remains Action Required.

tasks.title: Report and track: submit the complete NCRP financial-fraud complaint
tasks.user_goal: Create the national portal complaint, upload usable evidence and obtain a trackable reference.
tasks.trigger: After a 1930 call or directly when online filing is the fastest available path.

timelines.label: OTP validity
timelines.value: 30 minutes
timelines.applicability: NCRP citizen registration/login.

steps: Open https://cybercrime.gov.in using a trusted device and select the financial-fraud/other-cybercrime report-and-track route shown by the live portal.
Register/login with the victim's valid Indian mobile and OTP, select the victim's State/UT accurately, and enter the incident chronology.
Enter each bank/wallet/merchant, transaction ID/UTR, date and amount; upload the required identity and relevant evidence within current form limits.
Submit, save the on-screen confirmation, complaint reference, SMS/email and any evidence hash values.
tasks.tracking: Log in and use Check Status with the acknowledgement number; preserve status snapshots and communications.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct incomplete/invalid fields, retain rejected files, and use the portal's State/UT nodal/grievance contacts when response is not appropriate.
tasks.escalation: cf.t16 and cf.t17; an NCRP complaint is not itself proof of FIR conversion.

state_local_dependency.description: The selected State/UT police handles the complaint, FIR conversion and subsequent action under law.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The reference proves submission, not that a bank hold, FIR or investigation outcome exists.

tasks.title: Branch: pursue an unauthorised bank/card electronic-transaction claim
tasks.user_goal: Have the covered bank determine liability under the applicable RBI framework and produce a reasoned written outcome.
tasks.trigger: The user did not approve the electronic bank/card transaction, subject to the covered institution and facts.

timelines.label: Third-party breach notice
timelines.value: Within 3 working days of bank communication: zero liability; 4-7 working days: capped liability; beyond 7: bank Board policy
timelines.applicability: Only third-party breach where deficiency lies neither with bank nor customer; working days follow home-branch schedule and exclude communication date.

timelines.label: Shadow reversal
timelines.value: Within 10 working days of customer notification
timelines.applicability: Unauthorised transaction under the applicable bank circular; provisional/value-dated credit is not a final liability finding.

timelines.label: Liability resolution
timelines.value: Bank Board policy, not exceeding 90 days from complaint
timelines.applicability: Applicable covered unauthorised bank transaction.

steps: Submit the unauthorised-transaction complaint using the bank's official 24x7 route and preserve the exact notification timestamp.
State whether credentials were shared and attach the transaction alert/statement without conceding liability beyond known facts.
Request the bank's classification, Board-approved customer-liability policy, provisional credit decision and final reasoned determination.
For a lost card, demand immediate block and retain the blocking confirmation.
tasks.tracking: Track the 10-working-day provisional-credit and 90-day outer resolution clocks from the bank's acknowledged notification/complaint date.
tasks.rejection_handling: Challenge unsupported customer-negligence or authorisation findings through the bank's grievance/nodal route with evidence; the bank bears the burden of proving customer liability under the cited framework.
tasks.escalation: cf.t18 and cf.t19 when eligible.

state_local_dependency.description: Bank liability assessment is separate from State/UT criminal investigation, although the bank may request police/NCRP records under its current policy.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Zero liability depends on the transaction being unauthorised and the applicable fault/reporting facts; it is never inferred solely from the word fraud.

tasks.title: Branch: pursue an unauthorised non-bank PPI/wallet claim
tasks.user_goal: Use the PPI issuer's mandated fraud-reporting and liability process for an unauthorised wallet/PPI debit.
tasks.trigger: An unauthorised debit from a non-bank-issued PPI, subject to PPI type and exclusions.

timelines.label: Third-party breach notice
timelines.value: Within 3 days: zero; 4-7 days: transaction value or Rs 10,000, whichever lower; beyond 7: issuer Board policy
timelines.applicability: Covered non-bank PPI third-party breach, excluding the date the issuer's communication was received.

timelines.label: Notional reversal
timelines.value: Within 10 days of notification
timelines.applicability: Covered unauthorised PPI transaction; not a final liability determination.

timelines.label: Resolution
timelines.value: Not more than 90 days
timelines.applicability: Covered unauthorised non-bank PPI complaint.

steps: Use the direct unauthorised-transaction option on the issuer's official app/homepage or its 24x7 website/SMS/email/dedicated toll-free route.
Obtain the immediate complaint number and confirmation of action to prevent further PPI transactions.
Request the issuer's Board policy, liability classification, notional-credit decision and final reasoned outcome.
tasks.tracking: The PPI issuer must provide specific complaint numbers and status tracking; preserve the issuer's published escalation matrix.
tasks.rejection_handling: Check whether the instrument is a bank-issued PPI or excluded PPI-MTS; route bank-issued PPI to cf.t07 and unresolved covered non-bank PPI service deficiency to cf.t19 when eligible.
tasks.escalation: cf.t18 and cf.t19.

state_local_dependency.description: PPI liability is a regulated-actor determination distinct from police recovery.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Confirm issuer and PPI category; excluded PPI-MTS and victim-authorised transfers cannot inherit these protections automatically.

tasks.title: Branch: request recovery action for a successful victim-authorised scam transfer
tasks.user_goal: Seek a hold, recall, beneficiary-bank coordination or fraud review without claiming a stop-payment or zero-liability right.
tasks.trigger: The user approved a successful transfer because of impersonation, deception, coercion or a fraudulent collect request.

timelines.label: Guaranteed reversal or recall
timelines.applicability: No universal current primary rule in this pack guarantees recovery of a successful victim-authorised scam transfer.

steps: Tell the bank/PSP exactly that the payment was approved because of deception; do not misstate it as no-user-approval.
Request the actor's available fraud hold, recall, beneficiary-bank contact, account restriction and written investigation process.
Give the regulated actor the NCRP/1930 reference when available and ask what additional police document it requires.
Continue the State/UT police and actor grievance tracks even if the payment system shows success.
tasks.tracking: Track actor and NCRP references separately; require written status instead of relying on verbal 'funds frozen' statements.
tasks.rejection_handling: If the actor rejects because the transaction was authenticated, request a reasoned written response addressing the fraud report and any available recovery action; do not convert this into a zero-liability claim without evidence.
tasks.escalation: cf.t16, cf.t18 and, for deficiency in service by a covered regulated entity, cf.t19 when eligible.

state_local_dependency.description: Tracing, criminal process and any legal release/restoration dependency are State/UT and case-specific.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Fraudulent inducement is serious but does not itself prove an unauthorised electronic transaction, successful recall or fund availability.

tasks.title: Branch: apply the RBI failed-transaction TAT only to a matching failure
tasks.user_goal: Obtain the mandated auto-reversal/compensation for a domestic payment that failed for a reason not attributable to the customer.
tasks.trigger: Account/PPI debited but the transaction did not complete, and the exact RBI row applies.

timelines.label: UPI/IMPS funds transfer
timelines.value: Auto-reversal latest T+1 calendar day; Rs 100/day beyond T+1
timelines.applicability: Domestic debit to originator with beneficiary not credited.

timelines.label: UPI merchant/card POS-CNP merchant confirmation failure
timelines.value: Auto-reversal T+5 calendar days; Rs 100/day beyond T+5
timelines.applicability: Domestic debit where merchant confirmation is not received; not a completed purchase dispute.

timelines.label: ATM cash not dispensed
timelines.value: Reversal within T+5 calendar days; Rs 100/day beyond T+5
timelines.applicability: Account debited but cash not dispensed.

timelines.label: PPI on-us failure
timelines.value: Reversal within T+1 calendar day; Rs 100/day beyond T+1
timelines.applicability: Beneficiary PPI not credited or merchant confirmation not received; off-us follows underlying rail.

steps: Obtain the bank/PSP's recorded final transaction status and identify the exact RBI Annex row.
Raise the complaint with the bank/PSP/app and quote transaction reference, date and failure condition.
Check for automatic principal reversal and suo-moto compensation after the applicable calendar-day deadline.
If the transaction was successful, leave this branch and use cf.t09 or the merchant/card dispute route.
tasks.tracking: T is the calendar date of transaction; verify the reversal credit date and separate principal from compensation.
tasks.rejection_handling: If app status and bank ledger differ, raise both a status complaint and regulated-actor grievance; treat NPCI's general 48-hour pending FAQ as an apparent conflict, not a substitute for the binding row.
tasks.escalation: cf.t18 and cf.t19 after the applicable higher guideline/30-day eligibility period under RB-IOS 2026.

state_local_dependency.description: Failed-transaction TAT is a payment-system rule, not a police recovery route.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A successful fraudulent transfer is not reclassified as failed to obtain a TAT remedy.

tasks.title: Channel branch: use UPI app/bank/NPCI complaint routing correctly
tasks.user_goal: Create a UPI dispute record with the customer-facing app and bank, using NPCI only for the functions its portal currently exposes.
tasks.trigger: A UPI transaction is involved.
steps: Raise/check the transaction complaint in the participating UPI app when that app supports the scenario.
Also notify the account-holding/remitter bank; NPCI instructed member banks to acknowledge customer complaints irrespective of the PSP app used.
For fraudulent/unidentified/unauthorised transactions, follow the NPCI complaint page's direction to the respective bank.
Use NPCI's complaint portal only for a supported product/scenario; save the CRN and continue with the member institution that is responsible for resolution.
tasks.tracking: Check the app/NPCI CRN and bank complaint separately; the NPCI portal says the member institution remains responsible for resolution.
tasks.rejection_handling: If one participant redirects the user, cite the bank's complaint acceptance duty and keep both refusal and complaint records.
tasks.escalation: cf.t18; cf.t19 only after determining the applicable NPCI/RBI/card-network or 30-day eligibility period under the 2026 Scheme.

state_local_dependency.description: UPI dispute routing is separate from NCRP/State police handling, though both may run concurrently.

tasks.fail_closed_note: NPCI receipt is not a recovery decision, and its public complaint form is not the stated fraud-redress route.

tasks.title: Channel branch: bank-transfer recall/status for RTGS, NEFT or IMPS
tasks.user_goal: Have the remitting bank trace status and attempt any available bank-to-bank recovery without promising revocation.
tasks.trigger: A credit-push bank transfer by RTGS, NEFT or IMPS is involved.

timelines.label: Successful fraud-transfer reversal
timelines.applicability: RTGS is final and irrevocable; no universal successful NEFT/IMPS fraud-recall timeline was verified.

steps: Ask the remitting bank for final status, beneficiary-bank details available to it, and an immediate fraud recall/hold request if its process permits.
For RTGS, recognize that the RBI FAQ describes payments as final and irrevocable; distinguish non-credit/failed status from successful credit.
Provide 1930/NCRP/police references when available and require a written bank disposition.
tasks.tracking: Use the UTR/reference and bank complaint number; request positive/final status rather than assuming non-credit.
tasks.rejection_handling: Escalate bank service failures internally; legal recovery from a credited beneficiary account remains case-specific.
tasks.escalation: cf.t16, cf.t18 and cf.t19 when eligible.

state_local_dependency.description: Police/legal process may be required after funds are credited; no national local-court release workflow is asserted.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A recall request is an attempt, not a right to reverse a completed credit-push transfer.

tasks.title: Telecom branch: block a compromised SIM and review mobile connections
tasks.user_goal: Stop telecom-account misuse and identify connections issued in the victim's name.
tasks.trigger: Unexpected loss of service, SIM-swap/porting signs, unknown connections, or phone/SIM theft.

timelines.label: TSP SIM block/reissue
timelines.applicability: Provider-specific first-party route and proof must be verified for the actual TSP.

steps: Contact the actual telecom service provider through its official app/site/store and request immediate SIM block plus a fraud flag.
Ask for a complaint/reference number and the identity requirements for a replacement SIM.
Use Sanchar Saathi's Know Mobile Connections in Your Name service to review and report unknown connections.
After restoring control, re-check bank and email recovery numbers before re-enabling financial access.
tasks.tracking: Track TSP complaint and Sanchar Saathi report independently.
tasks.rejection_handling: Escalate through the identified TSP's current grievance route; do not invent a universal number or reissue timeline.
tasks.escalation: cf.t14 if the handset is lost/stolen and cf.t16 if impersonation/theft requires police action.

state_local_dependency.description: SIM service is provider-specific; police dependency arises for device theft or criminal investigation.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Sanchar Saathi review does not itself block the compromised SIM; confirm the TSP action in writing.

tasks.title: Device-loss branch: block the lost/stolen handset through CEIR
tasks.user_goal: Block the handset IMEI across Indian networks and retain a trackable CEIR request.
tasks.trigger: The mobile handset is lost or stolen.

timelines.label: CEIR block after successful request
timelines.value: Within 24 hours
timelines.applicability: Successfully submitted lost/stolen handset block request; it does not guarantee recovery.

timelines.label: SMS availability on a re-issued SIM
timelines.value: After 24 hours of SIM activation
timelines.applicability: CEIR FAQ statement attributed to TRAI regulation; relevant because the CEIR OTP is sent to the re-issued primary number, not a universal TSP reissue SLA.

steps: File and retain the police report for the lost/stolen handset.
Obtain a duplicate SIM for the lost number from the TSP because CEIR sends OTP to the reissued primary number.
Submit IMEI/device, loss, police-report and identity details in the CEIR block form.
Save the Request ID and check status; unblock only after the found handset is back in the user's possession and police requirements are satisfied.
tasks.tracking: Use CEIR Request ID or supported police complaint number on the CEIR status page.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct missing IMEI/police/identity data; for a new lost phone never used with a SIM, contact the CEIR district nodal police officer as the form directs.
tasks.escalation: CEIR helpdesk and State/UT police; tracing/recovery is not guaranteed.

state_local_dependency.description: A police report is required and device recovery is handled with State/UT police.

tasks.fail_closed_note: IMEI blocking prevents network use after processing; it does not erase data, block financial accounts or guarantee device recovery.

tasks.title: Account/device branch: secure compromised digital access from a trusted environment
tasks.user_goal: Remove persistence that could cause further fraud while preserving material needed for investigation.
tasks.trigger: Credential sharing, remote-access installation, suspicious sessions, email takeover or device compromise.
steps: From a trusted device, use each provider's official account-recovery route to change unique passwords and revoke unknown sessions/recovery methods.
Remove bank access and payment permissions before re-enabling ordinary use; follow the bank's instructions for re-registration.
Preserve evidence before deleting apps, messages or resetting the device; if forensic examination may be required, ask the investigating officer or qualified responder first.
Do not pay an unsolicited recovery agent or install another remote-access tool.
tasks.tracking: Keep official provider confirmation emails and a list of revoked sessions/recovery changes.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the actual provider's official recovery escalation; no universal private-platform procedure is asserted.
tasks.escalation: cf.t16 for criminal evidence and provider-specific support for access recovery.

state_local_dependency.description: Forensic seizure or examination, if any, is a police/legal dependency and must be separately instructed.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Generic hardening cannot replace the actual provider's recovery instructions or a forensic preservation decision.

tasks.title: Police dependency: cooperate with the assigned State/UT law-enforcement authority
tasks.user_goal: Provide complete records, obtain police references when issued, and follow lawful case-specific instructions.
tasks.trigger: NCRP assignment, police contact, local complaint/FIR need, device theft, or bank request for police documentation.

timelines.label: FIR conversion/investigation/restoration
timelines.applicability: State/UT and case-specific; no national completion timeline is verified.

steps: Respond to the assigned State/UT police request with the NCRP reference and indexed evidence.
Ask what acknowledgement, diary number, FIR copy or statement record will be issued and retain what is actually provided.
Give devices/original evidence only against an appropriate receipt or documented instruction.
Ask for the investigating contact and the lawful process, if any, for restoration of held funds; do not assume a hold can be released directly by the bank.
tasks.tracking: Use the NCRP status plus police-issued references; record all requests and submissions.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use the NCRP State/UT nodal/grievance contact when portal response is not appropriate; local procedural remedies require local verification.
tasks.escalation: cf.t17; any court/legal remedy is outside this pack and requires qualified local advice.

state_local_dependency.description: Police and public order are State subjects; State/UT LEAs handle FIR conversion, investigation, chargesheets, arrest and complaint resolution.

tasks.fail_closed_note: NCRP submission cannot be represented as an FIR, and no police action or timeline is promised.

tasks.title: Track NCRP and escalate an inadequate portal response to the listed State/UT contact
tasks.user_goal: Maintain a current status record and use the portal's official grievance route without inventing jurisdiction.
tasks.trigger: A trackable NCRP complaint exists and status is unclear, stale or inadequate.
steps: Check status in NCRP using the acknowledgement/reference.
Save each material status change and any assigned police contact.
If response is not appropriate, use the current State/UT nodal/grievance contact listed by NCRP and include the reference and concise issue.
tasks.tracking: NCRP Check Status and the State/UT grievance correspondence.
tasks.rejection_handling: Verify the live nodal page before use because named officials can change; preserve bounced-email or failed-call evidence.
tasks.escalation: State/UT authority shown on the live NCRP page; no central override is inferred.

state_local_dependency.description: The portal provides state-specific nodal/grievance contacts for inappropriate response.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A portal status or grievance email does not prove fund availability or restoration.

tasks.title: Complaint escalation: obtain the regulated actor's written final position
tasks.user_goal: Convert calls and verbal assurances into a complete complaint record suitable for RBI CMS or documented closure.
tasks.trigger: Initial complaint exists, documents are requested, status is unclear, or the user disputes the actor's response.

timelines.label: PPI ordinary grievance resolution
timelines.value: Preferably within 48 hours and not later than 30 days
timelines.applicability: PPI issuer customer complaints under the PPI Master Direction; unauthorised-PPI liability has its separate 90-day outer framework.

timelines.label: Covered regulated entity internal review
timelines.value: All partly or wholly rejected complaints auto-escalated to the Internal Ombudsman within 20 days of receipt; final decision communicated within 30 days of receipt
timelines.applicability: Only regulated entities covered by the RBI Internal Ombudsman Directions, 2023; the customer does not complain directly to the Internal Ombudsman.

steps: Submit all requested non-secret supporting documents through the actor's official route and record delivery.
Escalate through the published grievance/nodal officer levels, retaining every acknowledgement and reply.
Request a written statement of final transaction status, liability/recovery decision, amount credited/held if any, reasons, and further appeal route.

For a covered regulated entity's partly or wholly rejected complaint, do not contact the Internal Ombudsman directly: check that the final response says the Internal Ombudsman examined the complaint, gives reasons, and advises the RBI Ombudsman/CMS/CRPC route.
Record the applicable RBI/NPCI/card-network complaint timeline because RB-IOS 2026 uses the higher applicable period or 30 days.
tasks.tracking: Use the actor complaint reference and published escalation matrix; for a covered regulated entity, track the 20-day Internal Ombudsman auto-escalation and 30-day final-communication clocks from the regulated entity's receipt, not an assumed date.
tasks.rejection_handling: If a document or complaint is returned, cure the stated defect and preserve both versions. A customer should not contact the Internal Ombudsman directly; if the covered entity's rejection omits the Internal Ombudsman examination statement, reasons or RBI Ombudsman/CMS/CRPC advice, preserve the omission and assess cf.t19 promptly.
tasks.escalation: cf.t19 for covered RBI regulated entities when maintainable; State/UT police continues independently.

state_local_dependency.description: This is the regulated actor's internal grievance track.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Internal escalation does not extend the 90-day RBI Ombudsman filing window; calculate that window separately.

tasks.title: RBI escalation: assess and file under RB-IOS 2026 through CMS
tasks.user_goal: File a maintainable deficiency-in-service complaint against a covered RBI regulated entity within the current 2026 window.
tasks.trigger: The regulated entity gave an unsatisfactory reply/resolution, or gave no reply by 30 days or the longer applicable RBI/NPCI/card-network timeline.

timelines.label: Earliest no-reply filing point
timelines.value: After 30 days or the applicable longer RBI/NPCI/card-network timeline, whichever is higher
timelines.applicability: No reply; an unsatisfactory reply/resolution can enable filing without waiting for expiry, subject to the Scheme.

timelines.label: Ombudsman filing window
timelines.value: Within 90 days after that timeline expires or the last regulated-entity communication, whichever is later
timelines.applicability: Complaint to the regulated entity must also have been made within the Limitation Act period.

timelines.label: Appeal
timelines.value: Only against an Award; 30 days from receipt, with possible further period up to 30 days for sufficient cause
timelines.applicability: RB-IOS 2026 award appeal, not a general appeal from every closure/rejection.

steps: Confirm the respondent is covered by RB-IOS 2026 and the complaint alleges deficiency in service rather than only demanding police recovery; a suggestion, request for guidance or dispute showing no deficiency is not maintainable under the Scheme.

Check duplicate-forum maintainability: the same grievance pending before or decided by a court, tribunal, arbitrator or other judicial/quasi-judicial forum is excluded, but a criminal proceeding or police investigation is not treated as the same grievance for this exclusion.
Confirm proof of prior complaint, applicable higher timeline, latest reply date and the 90-day filing deadline.
File at https://cms.rbi.org.in, email crpc@rbi.org.in, or send the signed complaint/supporting documents to CRPC, RBI, Central Vista, Sector 17, Chandigarh 160017.
Save the RBI complaint number, track in CMS, respond to requests, and preserve the final communication.
If an Award is issued, decide acceptance/appeal within the stated period; do not promise an appeal from a non-appealable rejection.
tasks.tracking: CMS complaint number plus mobile number; Contact Centre 14448 provides guidance/status assistance but is not a filing channel.
tasks.rejection_handling: Cure incomplete data only if still within time; use the reasoned closure to identify other lawful remedies. A pending police investigation does not itself create the duplicate-forum bar, but it also does not prove deficiency in service.
tasks.escalation: Award appeal only when the 2026 Scheme permits; other legal remedies are outside this pack.

state_local_dependency.description: RB-IOS is jurisdiction-neutral; police investigation remains a separate State/UT track.

tasks.fail_closed_note: RBI CMS addresses deficiency in service by covered entities; it is not a police fund-recovery portal and does not guarantee compensation or reversal.

tasks.title: Outcome: prove restoration/reversal or preserve documented closure
tasks.user_goal: End the journey with verifiable money movement and written dispositions, or a clear unresolved/closed record for further advice.
tasks.trigger: Any actor reports a hold, reversal, restoration, rejection, settlement, award or closure.

timelines.label: CFCFRMS restoration/lien-removal citizen timeline
timelines.applicability: The 2026 SOP/MRM/GRM exists, but a public universal citizen workflow and completion time were not verified.

steps: Reconcile every claimed credit to the actual bank/PPI statement and original transaction reference.
Obtain the bank/issuer's final liability and complaint disposition, police/NCRP status, and RBI final communication where applicable.
Do not treat lien/hold, provisional shadow/notional credit, or verbal assurance as final restored funds.
Prepare a closure ledger listing recovered, provisionally credited, held, rejected and unresolved amounts plus remaining legal/action gates.
tasks.tracking: Retain statements and written dispositions for the limitation period or longer if proceedings continue; exact retention is case-specific.
tasks.rejection_handling: If actors disagree, keep the case open as Conflict and seek qualified legal/local advice rather than reporting a false completion.
tasks.escalation: Any further court, consumer, civil, insurance or professional recovery route is outside this pack and requires fact-specific advice.

state_local_dependency.description: Held-fund restoration may depend on State/UT police and legal process under the 2026 SOP.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Completion requires a matching statement credit and written disposition, or documented closure; partial hold and pending status remain Action Required.

tasks.title: Conditional device branch: contain a suspected malicious Android APK
tasks.user_goal: Stop a currently suspected malicious Android app from communicating while preserving available incident evidence and reporting financial activity.
tasks.trigger: The victim installed a suspected malicious RTO/eChallan-themed or materially similar Android APK associated with the incident.
steps: If safe and it will not delay active containment, preserve the message, URL, APK/app name, permissions, screenshots and timestamps; do not interact further with the sender.
Disconnect the affected phone from mobile data and Wi-Fi, uninstall the suspicious app and scan with a trusted antivirus product.
From a trusted environment where practicable, change relevant passwords and UPI PIN, check bank statements and report unusual account activity through the bank's official channel.
Report the incident through 1930/NCRP and retain the bank and NCRP references.
tasks.tracking: Record containment, uninstall, scan, credential-change and bank/NCRP report timestamps; keep any scan finding and official acknowledgement.
tasks.rejection_handling: If the app cannot be removed, the device remains abnormal or evidence/police preservation needs are unclear, keep it disconnected and seek qualified device incident-response or investigating-officer direction; do not improvise a destructive reset.
tasks.escalation: cf.t02 for financial containment, cf.t06 for NCRP filing, cf.t16 for assigned State/UT police procedure and cf.t20 for documented outcome.

state_local_dependency.description: CERT-In supplies a national technical containment baseline; forensic seizure or criminal investigation remains case-specific and State/UT dependent.

tasks.fail_closed_note: This branch is verified only for the cited malicious-APK fact pattern; these steps do not prove the device forensically clean, attribution, a bank hold or recovery. Evidence capture must not delay disconnecting an actively harmful device.

Regulated actor supplies status and acknowledgement.
Use any 1930 acknowledgement/instruction in online filing.

Preserve evidence before destructive remediation when safe.

The device-remediation and reporting log contributes to the documented case outcome; it does not prove forensic cleanliness or fund recovery.

National ID image in the currently stated format/size

portal_journeys.exception_route: Use 1930 for immediate financial fraud; if portal response is not appropriate, use the current State/UT nodal/grievance contact at https://www.cybercrime.gov.in/webform/Crime_NodalGrivanceList.aspx.

demo_scenario.title: SBI UPI collect-request scam reported within minutes - victim-authorised, no-guarantee demo
demo_scenario.purpose: Demonstrate urgent containment and reporting while refusing to misclassify a successful user-approved UPI scam as automatically zero-liability or reversible.
assumptions: On 2026-08-28 at 14:05 IST, a Bengaluru resident approves an SBI-linked UPI collect request for Rs 64,500 in a genuine UPI app after a caller falsely describes it as a refund-verification step.
The app and SBI alert show the payment as successful; the user entered the UPI PIN, so this pack treats it as victim-authorised pending a reasoned actor determination.
At 14:09 IST the user recognizes the scam, still controls the phone and SIM, and has no evidence of a second debit.
SBI is the remitter bank; the exact UPI app/PSP and beneficiary bank must be resolved from the transaction record before their channel-specific tasks are complete.
The user has transaction ID/UTR, alert, caller number, call log and chat screenshot, but no promise that funds remain in the beneficiary account.
All outcomes are illustrative; no hold, reversal, zero liability, FIR or recovery is assumed.

qualifier_answers.answer: Fraud has stopped but is recent; urgent containment starts at 14:09 IST.
One Rs 64,500 transaction at 14:05 IST; exact UTR is available in the SBI alert/app.
User approved because deceived and entered the UPI PIN.
UPI linked to an SBI savings account; app/PSP and beneficiary bank to be resolved.
Successful and credited according to current app/bank status.
No telecom issue known; phone and SIM remain controlled.
No OTP/password sharing or remote-access app known; UPI PIN was entered only in the real app.
No complaint at 14:09; first use SBI official containment/reporting and record ticket timestamp.
Only verbal/unknown until statement and written actor status prove otherwise.

out_of_scope_facts: No SIM swap or lost handset, so cf.t13 and cf.t14 are not used unless new facts emerge.
No failed-transaction status, so cf.t10's T+1/T+5 auto-reversal rules do not apply.
No no-user-approval debit, so cf.t07 and cf.t08 are not treated as the happy path.
No malicious APK or device compromise is known, so cf.t21 is not used unless new facts emerge.
No court, consumer commission, civil suit, insurance or private recovery-agent engagement is modelled.
action_required_gates: At about 14:09, call SBI 1800 1111 09 for fraud reporting and/or 1800 1234 -> 0 -> 3 for UPI block, obtain ticket and confirmation; request any available fraud hold/recall without assurance.

Call 1930 immediately and then complete NCRP with the UTR, amount, timestamp, SBI, suspect number and evidence; current national 24-hour mandate is not asserted, so file in the same urgent session where possible.
Resolve the actual UPI app/PSP and beneficiary bank from records; raise the app/bank complaint, recognizing NPCI routes fraud complaints to the bank and initiated UPI payments cannot be stopped.
Require SBI's written classification and recovery/service response; do not claim RBI zero liability because the user approved the payment.
If SBI gives an unsatisfactory response, or no response by the higher applicable guideline/30-day period, calculate the RB-IOS 2026 90-day filing window and file CMS promptly.
Treat a hold, provisional credit or verbal recovery statement as pending until an actual statement credit and written disposition exist.
demo_scenario.non_universality_note: The scenario is deliberately bounded to a successful victim-authorised SBI-linked UPI payment in Karnataka on 2026-08-28. Change of bank, app/PSP, rail, card network, transaction status, user-authorisation facts, State/UT or device/SIM facts changes the graph and may change the available remedies.
